name: PCOS (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome)
overview: PCOS is a common hormone condition in women of reproductive age. The ovaries may make more male-type hormones (androgens) than usual, and ovulation can become irregular.
signs: Extra hair on face or body
causes: The exact cause is not fully known. Insulin resistance, genes and hormone imbalance all play a part.
care: Doctors often suggest regular exercise, a balanced diet, weight management if needed, and medicines matched to your main concern (periods, acne or fertility). Do not start medicines on your own.
see_doctor: Periods missing for 3 months or more, very irregular cycles, trouble conceiving after 12 months of trying (6 months if you are 35 or older), or fast-worsening hair growth or acne.

name: Anemia (low hemoglobin)
overview: Anemia means the blood has fewer red blood cells or less hemoglobin than needed, so the body gets less oxygen. Iron deficiency is the most common cause in women.
causes: Too little iron in food, heavy periods, pregnancy, low B12 or folate, worm infections, or long-term illness.
care: Iron-rich foods (green leafy vegetables, legumes, jaggery, dates, and meat or eggs if you eat them) with vitamin C foods help. Tea or coffee right after meals can reduce iron absorption. The doctor may prescribe iron tablets after tests.
see_doctor: Breathlessness at rest, chest pain, fainting, very heavy periods, or if you are pregnant.

name: Endometriosis
overview: Tissue similar to the womb lining grows outside the womb, for example on the ovaries or pelvis. It can cause pain and sometimes trouble getting pregnant.
signs: Pain with urine or bowel movements during periods
causes: Not fully understood. Hormones and how the body responds to them play a role, and it often runs in families.
care: Pain-relief medicines, hormonal treatment and sometimes surgery, chosen by a gynecologist. Heat packs and gentle exercise may ease discomfort.
see_doctor: Period pain that stops you from daily activities, pain that keeps getting worse, or trouble conceiving.

name: Thyroid disorders
overview: The thyroid is a small gland in the neck that controls how the body uses energy. An underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism) is common in women. An overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism) is less common.
signs: Underactive: tiredness, weight gain, feeling cold, dry skin, constipation, heavy or irregular periods, low mood
Overactive: weight loss, fast heartbeat, sweating, anxiety, shaky hands, lighter periods
causes: Autoimmune conditions (such as Hashimoto's and Graves' disease), iodine imbalance, some medicines, and changes after pregnancy.
care: Diagnosed with blood tests (TSH, T4). An underactive thyroid is usually treated with a daily thyroid hormone tablet. Take it exactly as advised. Overactive thyroid has other treatment options.
see_doctor: Swelling in the neck, palpitations, marked weight change, or if you are planning a pregnancy.

name: Gestational diabetes
overview: High blood sugar that is first found during pregnancy, usually tested between 24 and 28 weeks (earlier if you are at higher risk). It often goes away after delivery but needs care to keep mother and baby healthy.
causes: Pregnancy hormones make the body less responsive to insulin. Risk is higher with overweight, a family history of diabetes, PCOS, or older age.
care: Balanced meals, regular walking as advised, checking blood sugar, and sometimes insulin or tablets. Your care team sets your targets. Get tested again after delivery, because the chance of type 2 diabetes later is higher.
see_doctor: Attend every scheduled test. Seek help for severe thirst, blurred vision, vomiting, or if the baby moves less.

name: Menopause
overview: Menopause is when periods have stopped for 12 months in a row. It usually happens between 45 and 55. The years before, when cycles change, are called perimenopause.
causes: A natural fall in estrogen and progesterone. It can also follow surgery that removes the ovaries or some cancer treatments.
care: Regular exercise, calcium and vitamin D, and not smoking help. For troublesome symptoms, doctors may discuss options, including hormone therapy, after weighing the benefits and risks for you.
see_doctor: Any bleeding after periods have stopped for a year, severe symptoms, or symptoms before age 40.

name: Breast health
overview: Most breast lumps are not cancer, but any new lump should be checked. Knowing how your breasts normally look and feel helps you notice changes early.
signs: Nipple turning inward or bloody discharge
Redness or rash that does not settle
causes: Age, family history and some hormonal factors raise risk. Many women with breast cancer have no clear risk factor.
care: Regular breast self-awareness, a clinical breast exam by a doctor, and screening (such as mammography) at the ages your doctor advises. Finding changes early improves outcomes.
see_doctor: Any new lump or change listed above. Do not wait for pain.

name: Urinary tract infection (UTI)
overview: A UTI is an infection of the bladder or urine passage. It is common in women because the urethra is shorter.
causes: Bacteria, mostly from the gut, entering the urinary tract. Risk rises with pregnancy, menopause, dehydration, and holding urine for long.
care: Drink enough water, do not hold urine, wipe front to back, and pass urine after intercourse. Most infections need antibiotics prescribed by a doctor after a urine test.
see_doctor: Fever, back or side pain, vomiting, blood in urine, symptoms during pregnancy, or symptoms that do not improve.
